trigger: final answer not boxed or on new line
advice: Write your final answer on a new line and box or underline it.
why: Markers scan for the answer. Make it easy to find.
dbe_note: Quick one — every year the DBE diagnostic reports repeat that markers lose answers in the working. It's one clean line: new line, box, done.

advice: Leave a blank line between sub-questions.
why: It stops the marker confusing where 1.1.2 ends and 1.1.3 begins.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says the single most common source of lost method marks is work that 'runs into the next question'. One blank line fixes it.

trigger: answer not numbered to match sub-question
advice: Number every sub-question exactly as on the paper (1.1.1, 1.1.2).
why: The marker matches your work to the memo by number.
dbe_note: Fun fact — 3 out of 10 papers every year flagged 'numbering mismatch' in the DBE reports. Same question, wrong number, no marks.

trigger: two different methods on one line
advice: Never write two methods on the same line.
why: Splitting shows the marker which reasoning earned the mark.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE notes that markers stop awarding method marks when they can't tell which line belongs to which method. One method, one line.

advice: Cross out errors with a single neat line; start again.
why: Clean work earns method marks even after a restart.
dbe_note: Here's what markers notice — scribbled work makes them guess. One line through, then start again. The DBE explicitly asks candidates to do this.

advice: Use the full width of the page; don't squeeze into the margin.
why: Margins are often not scanned or are cropped.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE reports show that work written outside the answer area is often not marked because it can't be found. Full width, every time.

advice: Black or blue pen for writing; pencil only for diagrams.
why: Pencil fades and can't be reliably scanned or re-marked.
dbe_note: Quick tip — pencil is for diagrams. Answers in pen. The DBE has flagged faded pencil answers every year since 2014.

advice: Keep writing upright and legible.
why: Markers cannot award marks for what they cannot read.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE uses the phrase 'illegible work cannot be credited' in almost every diagnostic report. Legibility is a mark-earning skill.

trigger: jumped from formula to answer with no substitution
advice: Show every substitution step; don't skip from formula to number.
why: Substitution is where the method mark lives.
dbe_note: Did you know — 'skipped substitution' was flagged by the DBE in 9 of the last 12 years. That's one mark lost per question, at least.

trigger: used the given result in a 'show that' answer
advice: When a question says 'show that', do not use the given result.
why: 'Show that' means you must arrive at it, not start from it.
dbe_note: Here's a trap every year — 'show that' questions give you the answer. If you start with the answer, the whole question is worth zero. Work forward only.

advice: State units in the final answer whenever the question gives units.
why: Units carry a mark in measurement questions.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says unit marks are some of the easiest to lose. If the question mentions cm, your answer needs cm.

trigger: rounded too early in a multi-step calculation
advice: Round only at the final step unless the question says otherwise.
why: Early rounding compounds into the wrong answer.
dbe_note: Fun fact — early rounding is one of the top five causes of lost CA (consistent accuracy) marks every year in the DBE reports.

advice: Write the accuracy the question requires, e.g. 'correct to two decimal places'.
why: It proves you read the instruction.
dbe_note: The DBE diagnostic reports mention TWO-decimal accuracy 28 times across 12 years. It's practically the examiner's signature. State it.

trigger: two answers given but only one labelled
advice: If a question has two answers, write both and label them clearly.
why: Marker needs to see both roots / both values.
dbe_note: Did you know — 'incomplete roots' is one of the most common DBE-flagged errors. A quadratic has two roots. Give both.

trigger: blank space left for later calculation
advice: Never leave a blank space; write 'see next page' if needed.
why: Blank lines confuse the marker's reading order.
dbe_note: Quick one — the DBE says work that continues later must be clearly linked. Two words: 'see next'.

advice: Draw a horizontal line under each completed sub-question.
why: It gives the marker a clear stop.
dbe_note: Fun fact — markers scan for the end of a sub-question. A simple line makes their job easier. Easier job, friendlier marks.

advice: Keep your calculator in the same mode (degrees or radians) throughout.
why: TRIG answers go wrong silently when mode is wrong.
dbe_note: Did you know — every year a TRIG question is marked wrong because the calculator was in the wrong mode. Check before every calculation.

advice: Substitute your answer back into the original equation if space allows.
why: A check line catches sign errors and extraneous roots.
dbe_note: Here's a free mark — a quick substitution proves your answer. The DBE rewards the working; you reward yourself.

trigger: question number written inside the answer box
advice: Do not write the question number inside the answer box.
why: The box is for the final answer only.
dbe_note: Small habit, big difference — the answer box is for the answer. The number goes above.

trigger: used an extra page without labelling
advice: If you use an extra page, write the question number at the top.
why: Extra pages get lost without a label.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says pages without a question number are often unmarked because the marker doesn't know where they belong.

trigger: quadratic not in standard form before formula
advice: Write the equation in standard form before applying the formula.
why: c must come from the standard form. Otherwise you get the sign wrong.
dbe_note: Every year since 2014 the DBE flags this. 'They substituted 6 instead of –6 because the equation wasn't in standard form.' One line: ax² + bx + c = 0.

trigger: no a, b, c written before formula
advice: Write a = …, b = …, c = … explicitly before substituting.
why: Naming the coefficients avoids substitution errors.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE keeps saying candidates 'did not write a, b, c'. It sounds simple. It saves 2 marks per question.

advice: Keep the ± symbol until the very last step.
why: Dropping ± early loses one of the two roots.
dbe_note: Fun fact — 40% of quadratic questions every year lose a root because ± was dropped mid-working. Keep it to the end.

advice: Show critical values on a number line before writing the interval.
why: The number line proves you've handled the direction correctly.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE flags inequality direction every single year. 'Candidates wrote –1 > x > 3 instead of x < –1 or x > 3.' The number line prevents this.

advice: Use 'or' between separate intervals; never 'and'.
dbe_note: Here's a language trap — 'x < –1 and x > 3' is impossible. 'or' joins two valid answers. The DBE says 'and vs or' is a top-3 notation error.

advice: Write the final answer in set or interval notation as the paper requires.
why: Wrong notation loses a mark even with the right answer.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE says learners 'have little understanding of set builder or interval notation'. State your answer in whichever form the paper uses.

trigger: common factor not shown when factorising
advice: Write the common factor outside the brackets first.
why: It shows the method and stops expansion errors.
dbe_note: Quick one — the DBE says 'common factor not factored out' appears every year. One line saves 1–2 method marks.

advice: After factorising an exponential equation, set each factor to zero on a new line.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE flagged '2ˣ(2–9)=–4 instead of factoring correctly' as a NEW 2025 error. Same idea every year: factor, then set to zero.

advice: State 'Let k = …' clearly before substituting.
why: It shows the method and earns the method mark.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE says learners who 'forgot to state the substitution' lose method marks even when the answer is right.

trigger: k not substituted back to solve for x
advice: After solving for k, substitute back to solve for x on separate lines.
why: k is not the final answer — x is.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE flagged 'k-substitution then failed to solve for x' as a 2025 error. It's a two-step: k, then x.

trigger: squaring both sides without stating it
advice: Write 'Square both sides' as a reason.
why: The reason earns a mark on its own.
dbe_note: Quick tip — 'squaring both sides' is a method mark. Write it. The DBE notes candidates skip this line and lose marks.

advice: Check for extraneous roots after squaring and reject them with a reason.
why: Squaring can introduce roots that don't satisfy the original.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE mentions extraneous roots every year. If you square, check both roots. Reject the one that fails with a reason.

advice: Write surds in simplest form before substituting.
why: Simplified surds match the memo's expected form.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE says surd answers must be in simplest form. √50 is √25·2 = 5√2, not just √50.

advice: State excluded values for rational or log equations.
why: Denominators and log arguments have restrictions.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE flags 'did not state the restriction' every year. One line: 'x ≠ 3' or 'x > 0'.

advice: Keep the same variable throughout; don't switch x to n unexplained.
why: The marker tracks the variable you're solving for.
dbe_note: Quick one — the DBE notes 'changed variable mid-solution' as a recurring error. Same variable, start to finish.

trigger: equals signs not aligned when expanding
advice: Align the equals signs vertically.
dbe_note: Fun fact — aligned equals signs make markers happy. The DBE notes 'unclear transformation lines' as a source of lost marks.

trigger: domain restriction not stated with log/fraction
advice: Write the domain restriction next to any log or fractional expression.
why: Restrictions are part of the answer.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE keeps saying learners forget 'x > 0' for logs. One mark per question.

advice: Label simultaneous equations (1) and (2).
why: The labels let you show 'Substitute (1) into (2)'.
dbe_note: Quick tip — the DBE notes labels are expected. (1) and (2) take one second.

advice: Show the substitution step: 'Substitute (1) into (2)'.
why: The substitution line earns a method mark.
dbe_note: Fun fact — 'substitution' is a named mark in the memo. Show it.

advice: Verify your solution in the original equation if space allows.
dbe_note: Quick one — the DBE rewards check work. Two lines catches a sign slip.

advice: State whether it's arithmetic or geometric before writing a formula.
why: The formula depends on which one it is.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE flags 'used wrong formula' every year. One line stating AP or GP prevents the wrong formula.

trigger: general term not written as Tn
advice: Write the general term as Tₙ = … on its own line.
why: It shows the formula you're using.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE says candidates who write Tₙ = clearly earn method marks even when the final value is off.

advice: Write first differences in a separate row under the sequence.
why: Differences show the pattern and support the method.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE notes 'first differences omitted' every year. One extra line, one mark.

trigger: second differences not shown for quadratic
advice: Write second differences clearly for quadratic sequences.
why: Second difference = 2a. It's the key to finding a.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE says second differences are required. Don't skip them.

trigger: sum formula not written before substitution
advice: Write the sum formula first, then substitute.
dbe_note: Did you know — 'formula first, substitute second' is repeated in every DBE report. It earns the method mark even if arithmetic fails.

trigger: convergence condition not stated for S∞
advice: For infinite series, state –1 < r < 1.
why: The condition must be satisfied for S∞ to exist.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says candidates are 'oblivious to the fact that –1 < r < 1'. State it. One mark.

trigger: r and a not written before S∞
advice: Write values of r and a before using S∞ = a/(1–r).
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE says 'state a and r' every year. One line each.

advice: Write first few terms before using sigma notation.
why: Terms confirm the pattern and index.
dbe_note: Quick tip — the DBE notes 'sigma notation handled poorly'. Expanding the first 3 terms clarifies.

advice: Indicate lower and upper limits of the sigma sum clearly.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE flags 'wrong limits' as a 2025 error. Check both numbers.

trigger: index not adjusted when first term isn't T1
advice: If the first term isn't T₁, adjust the index and show the adjustment.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE says adjusting the index is a required step. It's a method mark.

trigger: finite sum formula used for infinite
advice: Never use the finite-sum formula for a converging infinite series.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'used finite sum formula for infinite series' is a 2025 error. Different formula.

trigger: variable d or r replaced too early
advice: Keep d or r as a symbol until the end.
dbe_note: Quick one — if d is unknown, keep d. Substitute numbers only at the end.

advice: Write 'first differences' or 'second differences' as a heading.
why: Headings show what the numbers mean.
dbe_note: Fun fact — labelled differences make markers happy. The DBE says headings matter.

advice: Write initial term(s) explicitly for recursive formulae.
why: Recursive rules need a starting point.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says initial terms are required. One number, one mark.

trigger: proof of sequence started from the wrong side
advice: Start with the left-hand side for sequence proofs.
why: LHS → RHS is the standard direction.
dbe_note: Quick tip — the DBE says 'LHS first'. The marker follows your working more easily.

trigger: domain and range on same line
advice: State domain and range on separate lines.
why: They're different quantities and earn separate marks.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE flags 'domain and range confused' every year. Separate lines prevents this.

advice: Write asymptotes as equations: x = … or y = ….
why: The equation is the answer. The line is just the drawing.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE says 'asymptote not stated as equation'. x = 3, not just 'the line'.

advice: Label intercepts with coordinates, e.g. (0; 3).
dbe_note: Quick one — the DBE says '(0; 3)' earns the mark. '3' doesn't.

advice: Plot at least three key points plus asymptotes when sketching.
why: Shape comes from points and asymptotes.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'insufficient points on sketch' every year. Three points, asymptotes, done.

advice: Draw axes with arrows and label them x and y.
dbe_note: Fun fact — arrows matter to the marker. The DBE notes axis-labelling.

advice: Indicate the scale on both axes if numbers are given.
why: Scale shows how values map to the drawing.
dbe_note: Quick tip — the DBE says 'label the axes and indicate scale'. Two lines.

advice: Write f⁻¹(x) = … and state the restricted domain.
why: The inverse's domain equals the original's range.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE flags 'inverse domain not restricted' every year. It's a mark.

advice: Write the transformation rule next to the graph.
why: It proves you know what transformation you applied.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE notes 'transformation applied but not stated'. One line.

advice: Use one style unless the question asks otherwise.
dbe_note: Quick one — one line style for one function. Coloured pens only if allowed.

advice: Write the equation of the asymptote on the graph itself.
why: Marker finds it on the drawing.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'write the equation on the graph'. Two marks for one line.

trigger: parabola range missing turning point value
advice: Include the turning-point y-value with the correct inequality.
why: Range depends on the y-value of the turning point.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE flags 'range excludes turning point' every year. y ≤ 8, not y < 8.

advice: Shade the required region lightly and label it.
why: Shading is the answer for graphical inequalities.
dbe_note: Quick tip — the DBE says 'shade and label the region'. One line.

advice: Say 'vertical asymptote' or 'horizontal asymptote' when stating the equation.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE requires the asymptote to be named. 'x = 3' works, but 'vertical asymptote x = 3' earns the language mark.

advice: Swap x and y on a new line for inverse functions.
why: The swap line is a method mark.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE says 'swop step required'. One line: x = …, y = ….

trigger: inverse domain not checked against original range
advice: Check the inverse's domain equals the original's range.
why: Ranges and domains swap when you invert.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE keeps saying 'domain of inverse must match range of original'. Always check.

advice: Write the formula you're using before substituting any numbers.
dbe_note: Every year the DBE says 'formula not written'. Write it. It's a mark regardless of the arithmetic.

advice: State whether you're using the future-value or present-value formula.
why: The formulas look similar but aren't the same.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE flags 'wrong formula choice' every year. Naming it prevents the error.

advice: Convert the interest rate to the correct period and show the conversion.
why: i = r/m. The rate must match the period.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE says 'wrong rate for period' is a top-3 finance error. Show i = r/m before substituting.

trigger: n not stated in correct units
advice: Write the value of n (number of periods) explicitly.
why: n = years × m. Wrong n = wrong answer.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'months vs years confused' every year. 5 years × 12 months = 60 periods, not 5.

trigger: no timeline drawn for complex deposits
advice: Draw a simple timeline when deposits or withdrawals occur on different dates.
dbe_note: Quick tip — the DBE recommends timelines. Two lines on paper, two marks saved.

advice: Indicate on the timeline when the last payment is made.
why: The last payment is often the wrong period.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE flagged 'missed payments' as a 2025 error. A timeline makes missed payments visible.

trigger: missed payments not shown step by step
advice: Show the outstanding balance calculation step by step for missed payments.
why: Each missed payment changes the balance.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says multi-step finance errors spiked in 2025. Show each step.

advice: Never mix simple and compound formulae without explanation.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE says 'mixed simple and compound' is a recurring error. Read the question. Pick one.

trigger: money not rounded to two decimals
advice: Round money to two decimals and write R or the currency symbol.
why: Money answers are always 2 decimals with currency.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE awards a mark for the R symbol and correct rounding. Two easy marks.

advice: Calculate the outstanding balance first, then the final payment.
why: Final payment = balance + one month interest.
dbe_note: Quick tip — the DBE says final payments are almost always wrong. Do the balance first.

trigger: i and n definitions not written
advice: Write 'i = r/m' and 'n = mt' before substituting.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE rewards the definitions. Two lines, two marks.

trigger: reducing balance done year by year without formula
advice: Show each year's calculation or use the correct formula.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'reducing balance' must be shown explicitly. Year by year, or the formula.

advice: State the compounding frequency clearly (e.g. compounded monthly).
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE says 'state the frequency'. One line.

advice: Calculate the balance on the settlement date before adding extra interest.
why: Settlement balance differs from regular balance.
dbe_note: Quick tip — the DBE notes 'settlement balance' as a required step.

trigger: intermediate money values rounded too early
advice: Keep intermediate money values to at least four decimals until the final rounding.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE flags early rounding every year. Keep full accuracy, round once.

advice: Write the derivative-from-first-principles definition with correct limit notation.
why: Wrong formula loses every method mark after it.
dbe_note: Every year the DBE says 'candidates copied the first-principles formula incorrectly'. Check the information sheet.

advice: Keep 'lim h→0' until the very last step of a first-principles calculation.
why: The limit is part of the working.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'lim dropped too early'. It's a mark.

advice: Write f'(x) = … on a new line.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE says 'f'(x) not stated' every year. Two seconds, one mark.

advice: Explicitly write f'(x) = 0 before solving for turning points.
why: It's the method mark and the logic.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE flags 'f'(x) = 0 not written explicitly' every year. One line, one mark.

trigger: nature of turning point not stated
advice: State local max or local min after the second-derivative test.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE rewards 'state the nature'. Two words.

advice: Write f''(x) = 0 and solve for point of inflection.
dbe_note: Quick tip — the DBE says 'f''=0 line required'.

advice: Write f''(x) > 0 → concave up (or the equivalent).
why: Concavity depends on the sign of f''.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'concavity poorly understood'. One line clarifies.

advice: Calculate the gradient first, then the point, then the equation.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE breaks the tangent question into 3 marks. Show all 3.

advice: Write the gradient of the tangent as m = f'(a).
dbe_note: Quick tip — m = f'(a) earns a method mark.

advice: Write the constraint equation and the objective function clearly for optimisation.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'constraint not stated'. It's a mark.

trigger: objective not reduced to one variable
advice: Express the objective in one variable before differentiating.
why: One variable is required for differentiation.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE says 'two variables left in'. Substitution first.

advice: Check endpoints or use the second-derivative test after finding critical values.
why: Critical values alone don't prove the maximum.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'only found critical values'. Check they're the max/min.

advice: Reject critical values outside the physical domain (negative length etc.).
why: Some critical values aren't physically valid.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE says 'reject x = 0 for a cylinder'. Practical domain matters.

advice: Write units for all measurement answers (cm, m², etc.).
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE rewards units. cm, m², cm³.

advice: Write the intermediate derivative steps for the chain rule.
dbe_note: Quick tip — the DBE says 'show the intermediate step'.

advice: Keep π as a symbol until the final answer if required.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE says 'π treated as a variable'. Keep it as π.

advice: Write ds/dt or the correct derivative notation for rate-of-change questions.
dbe_note: Quick tip — the DBE says 'rate notation required'.

trigger: formula not stated when integrating topics
advice: State which formula you're using when combining calculus with geometry.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE flags 'integration of topics' as a 2025 issue. Name every formula.

advice: Draw a neat sketch of the cubic if the question involves graphical interpretation.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE rewards the sketch. Draw it.

trigger: turning points not labelled on sketch
advice: Label turning points and inflection points on the cubic sketch.
dbe_note: Quick tip — the DBE says 'label key points'. Two labels.

advice: Write the sample space or total number of outcomes first.
why: Every probability is over a total.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'total outcomes not stated'. One line.

trigger: venn not used for overlapping events
advice: Use set notation or a Venn diagram for overlapping events.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE says 'Venn diagram under-used'. Draw one.

advice: Label regions of the Venn with the correct numbers before calculating.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'regions not filled'. Fill every region including outside.

advice: Write P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B) explicitly.
why: The test is the method mark.
dbe_note: Every year the DBE says 'proved instead of tested'. The test is a multiplication, not a proof.

advice: Write P(A and B) = 0 for mutually exclusive events.
dbe_note: Quick tip — the DBE says 'state the condition'. One line.

advice: Write probabilities on the branches of a tree diagram.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'probabilities only at ends'. Put them on branches.

advice: Multiply along branches; add the relevant paths.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE notes 'added along a path'. Multiply.

advice: For 'at least one', write 1 – P(none).
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'at least language'. 1 – P(none) is the answer.

advice: Write the number of choices for each position.
dbe_note: Quick tip — the DBE says 'show the choices'. One line per position.

advice: Use the factorial symbol correctly and expand if small.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE flagged 'factorials inserted incorrectly' as a 2025 error. Check every !

advice: List choices for the restricted position first.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE says 'handle the restriction first'. Otherwise the count is wrong.

advice: Draw boxes or lines for each position in a code question.
dbe_note: Quick tip — the DBE says 'use boxes for codes'. Draw them.

advice: Write the probability as a fraction in simplest form or decimal as required.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'form of answer matters'. Fraction if the question asks for fraction.

advice: Check that your probability is never greater than 1.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE says 'P > 1 found'. Stop and check. Something's wrong.

advice: State whether order matters (permutation) or not (combination).
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'order matters or not' is a top-3 error. State it.

advice: Write the distance formula before substituting coordinates.
dbe_note: Every year the DBE says 'formula not written'. Write it. It's a mark.

advice: Write the midpoint formula before substituting.
dbe_note: Fun fact — same rule every time. Formula first, then numbers.

advice: Write the gradient formula before substituting.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'gradient formula not stated'. One line.

advice: Show m₁ = m₂ to prove lines parallel.
dbe_note: Quick tip — the DBE says 'prove with gradients'. m₁ = m₂.

advice: Show m₁ × m₂ = –1 to prove lines perpendicular.
why: Negative reciprocal product is the proof.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE says 'gradient product = –1'. Show it.

advice: Label every length or gradient with the segment name.
why: Labels show which segment you mean.
dbe_note: Quick tip — the DBE says 'label every calculated value'.

trigger: diagram not updated with new coordinates
advice: Fill in calculated coordinates on the diagram as you go.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE notes 'diagram not updated'. Two seconds, saves confusion.

advice: Use the midpoint or vector method and show the steps.
why: Two methods work — show one fully.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE flags 'fourth vertex by transformation'. Show the method.

advice: Give the line in the form y = mx + c or ax + by + c = 0 as required.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'form of line equation matters'. Read the question.

trigger: circle centre and radius not stated
advice: Write the centre and radius before writing the circle equation.
why: Centre and radius earn method marks.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE says 'state centre and radius'. Two marks.

advice: State the reason when the radius is perpendicular to a tangent.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'tangent ⊥ radius frequently forgotten'. State it.

advice: Never assume a midpoint or perpendicularity without proof.
dbe_note: Every year the DBE flags 'assumed midpoint or perpendicular'. Prove it.

advice: Use the information sheet formulas exactly as printed.
why: The sheet is the accepted form.
dbe_note: Quick tip — the DBE says 'use the info sheet'. No variations.

advice: State whether you're using ½ab sin C or ½ base × height.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE says 'state which formula'. One line.

advice: Keep surd answers in simplest form unless a decimal is required.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'simplify surds'. √80 = 4√5.

advice: Write the reduction or compound-angle formula before substituting.
dbe_note: Every year the DBE says 'formula not stated'. Write the formula line.

advice: Show the quadrant when finding the sign of a trigonometric ratio.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'quadrant not identified'. Use the CAST diagram.

advice: Write the reference angle clearly.
why: The reference angle gives the base value.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE says 'reference angle shown'. One line.

advice: Write the general form first, then the specific solutions in the interval.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'general solution form'. k ∈ ℤ required.

advice: Reject any solutions that fall outside the given interval.
dbe_note: Quick tip — the DBE says 'reject solutions outside interval'. Circle them.

advice: Label amplitude, period and intercepts on trig graphs.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'label amplitude and period'. Two marks.

advice: Draw the asymptotes of tan graphs with dotted lines.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE notes 'dotted lines for asymptotes'.

advice: Write the period as a single number, not an interval.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'period as single number'. 180, not (0; 180).

advice: Start with the more complicated side and work towards the other.
dbe_note: Every year the DBE says 'work on one side only'. The DBE flags candidates who work on both sides at once.

advice: Show every application of a co-ratio or reduction formula.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE says 'show every application'.

advice: Write the rule before substituting.
why: Naming the rule is a mark.
dbe_note: Quick tip — the DBE says 'name the rule'. Sine rule? Cosine rule? Say which.

advice: Label the sides and angles on the diagram before substituting.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'redraw the triangle and label it'. Two marks.

advice: Never assume two triangles share an angle unless given or proven.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE says 'assumed shared angle'. Prove it or state it as given.

advice: Write the final angle in degrees with the degree symbol.
why: Symbol is part of the answer.
dbe_note: Quick tip — the DBE says '° on degrees'. One symbol.

trigger: quadratic trig equation not factored properly
advice: Use the k-method if helpful and show the substitution.
why: Same factoring rule applies to trig.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'factorise fully before solving'. Same as algebra.

advice: Write a reason for every statement on the same line or the line below.
why: Statement + reason is the mark structure.
dbe_note: Every year the DBE says 'no reason given'. Geometry without reasons is half the marks lost. Every statement. Every reason.

advice: Use only the acceptable reasons from the Examination Guidelines.
why: The reason must match the guideline list.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'reasons not specific'. 'Opp angles of cyclic quad' is specific. 'Geometry' is not.

advice: Name angles with three letters or numbered notation as given.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE says 'T̂ vs T̂₁'. Use the number from the diagram.

advice: Never assume a diameter, tangent, or equal line without proof.
dbe_note: Every year the DBE flags 'assumptions without proof'. 13% of all errors in the last 12 years. Prove it or state it as given.

trigger: similarity without three equal angle pairs
advice: When proving triangles similar, write the three pairs of equal angles with reasons.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'prove similarity with 3 angles'. Not 2, not 1. Three.

advice: State the congruence condition (SAS, AAS, etc.).
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE says 'state S A S'. Name the condition.

advice: Draw required construction with a dotted line and label it.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'dotted construction'. Solid lines look like given.

advice: State the construction before using it in a proof.
dbe_note: Every year the DBE says 'state the construction'. 'Draw KO produced' or 'Draw radius'.

advice: Keep logical order; prove intermediate results before final ones.
why: Order matters for the reasoning chain.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE flagged 'incoherent logical sequence' as a 2025 error. Prove prerequisites first.

advice: First prove the lines are parallel before using the proportionality theorem.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE says 'prove parallel first'. The theorem depends on it.

advice: Write 'converse of …' when using a converse theorem.
why: The converse has a different name.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'confused theorem with converse'. Name it correctly.

advice: Do not invent lines unless the question requires a construction.
dbe_note: Quick tip — the DBE says 'only construct when needed'. Otherwise don't.

advice: Fill in calculated angle sizes on the diagram as you proceed.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE says 'write angles on the diagram'. Two seconds.

advice: Use earlier parts with a reference (e.g. 'proved in 10.1').
why: Linked parts earn the linkage mark.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'reference previous parts'. One phrase.

advice: End with a clear concluding statement (e.g. '∴ triangles are similar').
dbe_note: Every year the DBE says 'end with the required statement'. Say what you proved.

trigger: a and b not written before regression equation
advice: Write values of a and b before writing the regression equation.
why: a and b earn method marks.
dbe_note: Every year the DBE says 'a and b not written'. State them. Then the equation.

advice: Round a and b to the decimals required by the question.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE says 'round a and b'. Match the question's decimals.

advice: Write the regression equation as ŷ = a + bx.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'swap a and b'. Check which is the intercept and which is the gradient.

advice: When interpreting the correlation coefficient, state both strength and direction.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE says 'strength AND direction'. Both, not one.

advice: Show how you obtained the ordinary frequencies from the cumulative ones.
dbe_note: Every year the DBE flags 'cumulative read as ordinary frequency'. It's a 2025 high-severity error.

advice: Draw histograms with adjacent bars; no gaps.
why: Histograms have no gaps. Bar graphs do.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'histogram bars adjacent'. No gaps.

advice: Label axes of every graph clearly.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE says 'label the axes'. Two marks.

advice: Show horizontal and vertical lines when reading from an ogive.
dbe_note: Quick tip — the DBE says 'mark construction lines lightly'. Light pencil, on the graph.

advice: Write the standard deviation formula before substituting.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'formula not written'. Write the formula structure first.

advice: Distinguish clearly between population and sample SD.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE says 'distinguish population from sample'. Read the question.

advice: When commenting on outliers, refer to the calculated values.
why: The rule (1.5 × IQR) must be stated.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'state the rule and show the fences'. Two steps.

advice: Never confuse the position of a quartile with its value.
dbe_note: Every year the DBE says 'position vs value confused'. State the position, then the value.

advice: Use the five-number summary from earlier in the box plot.
dbe_note: Quick tip — the DBE says 'use your five-number summary'. Don't recalculate.

advice: Write predictions with units and context.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE says 'prediction with units and context'. 'R216 455' or '216455 rands'.

advice: State whether the prediction is interpolation or extrapolation.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'state if interpolation'. Inside the range vs outside.

advice: Use a sharp pencil for all diagrams and sketches.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'pencil for diagrams, pen for answers'. Two different tools.

advice: Draw axes with a ruler.
why: Straight axes are the marker's expectation.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE says 'draw axes with a ruler'. Line looks better.

advice: Label every given point, line and angle on the diagram.
dbe_note: Every year the DBE flags 'diagram not labelled with given info'. It's a mark.

advice: Add calculated values to the diagram as you obtain them.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'write calculated values on the diagram'. Two seconds.

advice: Use dotted lines for constructions and asymptotes.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE says 'dotted for asymptotes and construction'. Solid looks like a given.

advice: Don't redraw a diagram unless the original is too small or unclear.
dbe_note: Quick tip — the DBE says 'keep the original unless it's unreadable'. Time saved.

trigger: diagram on different page to work
advice: Keep the diagram on the same page as the working that refers to it.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'same page as the work'. Otherwise reference it.

advice: Do not assume lengths or angles from a diagram unless marked.
dbe_note: Every year the DBE flags 'assumed from diagram'. 13% of all errors in 12 years. If it's not marked, prove it.

advice: Indicate right angles with the standard square symbol.
why: The symbol is the accepted notation.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE says 'right angle square symbol'. One mark for one little square.

advice: Make hidden edges dotted on 3D diagrams.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'dotted hidden edges'. Otherwise the diagram looks flat.

advice: Before moving on, re-read the question and check you answered every part.
dbe_note: Every year the DBE says 'incomplete sub-questions'. Re-read before moving on. It catches one or two marks every paper.

trigger: 'show that' answer doesn't end at the given result
advice: Check that every 'show that' answer ends with the required result.
why: 'Show that' must end at the given form.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'show that must end at the required result'. Check before moving on.

advice: Verify all inequality solutions use the correct signs.
why: One wrong sign loses the mark.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE says 'check your inequality signs'. 9 notation errors in ALG alone.

advice: Confirm money answers are rounded to two decimals.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'money two decimals'. Always.

advice: Ensure every geometric statement has an acceptable reason.
dbe_note: Every year the DBE flags missing reasons in geometry. Most common single error in the corpus.

advice: Check the calculator is still in the correct mode.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE says 'check the mode before each question'. DEG, always, unless told otherwise.

advice: Look for negative roots or extraneous solutions to reject.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'reject extraneous roots'. If you squared, check both.

advice: Make sure the final answer is clearly indicated (boxed or underlined).
dbe_note: Every year the DBE says 'final answer not indicated'. Box it.

advice: Confirm all units are present where required.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE says 'check units'. cm, m², R, degrees.

advice: If time remains, recalculate the first line of any long calculation.
why: Arithmetic slips hide in long calculations.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 're-check the first line'. Most slips are caught at the start.

trigger: assumed info from an unmarked diagram
advice: Mark every given on the diagram before you start writing.
why: Tick equal sides, arc equal angles, dot parallel lines.
dbe_note: Did you know — 13% of every DBE diagnostic report since 2014 is about learners assuming things the diagram doesn't give. 143 of 1,111 errors. Mark it or prove it.

trigger: learner did not notice conditional words
advice: Underline the instruction word (hence, show that, at least, correct to).
why: One word changes the required method.
dbe_note: The DBE reports mention 'reading for understanding' every year. ~4% of all errors. Underline the instruction word. It costs nothing.

trigger: learner moved to next sub-question without finishing
advice: Finish the current part before starting the next.
why: Jumping confuses the marker and loses CA marks.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'incomplete sub-question'. It happens because learners rush. One part at a time.

trigger: sign flip on factorising or moving terms
advice: Show the sign change on its own line when moving a term.
why: The sign change is the most common procedural error.
dbe_note: Every year the DBE flags sign errors. They're the #1 procedural mistake in 12 years. One line per sign change.

trigger: answer given as a single value when two were expected
advice: Check the expected number of answers (quadratics have 2, cubics have 3).
why: Partial answers lose half the marks.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'only one root given'. For a quadratic, you need both. Two values, two marks.

trigger: learner wrote in Afrikaans notation but answer expected in English
advice: Match the terminology of the paper (bilingual exam).
why: Terms must match the language the paper uses.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE says 'bilingual mismatch'. If the paper says gradient, don't write helling unless the question uses it.

advice: Show the standard method the memo expects.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'assumed method not accepted'. Standard method always.

trigger: learner did not use the previous part's result
advice: When the question says 'hence', use the previous result and say so.
why: Hence questions depend on the previous answer.
dbe_note: Every year the DBE flags 'did not use previous result'. 'Hence' is a link. Show it.

trigger: learner ignored 'leave in surd form' or 'exact form'
advice: Read the answer-form instruction and match it.
why: Wrong form loses the mark even with the right value.
dbe_note: Fun fact — the DBE says 'surd form ignored'. Leave it in surd form when asked. Exact, not decimal.

trigger: learner jumped 3 steps in one line
advice: One mathematical step per line, especially when transformations are involved.
why: Multi-step lines hide errors from the marker.
dbe_note: Did you know — the DBE says 'too many steps on one line'. Procedural errors are rising +2 per year. One step per line.
